clue.text: There is near mixture in tin in it

definitions.text: There is near mixture in tin in it

indicators.note: the second 'in' says the following pieces sit inside the word 'it'

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: a mixture is a jumble, so the letters of 'near' are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe-like remark about something blended into tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges the second word to give ERAN; the second 'in' puts the run inside the last word. The whole clue also describes a travelling tinker, who mends tin and never stays near one spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinker who wanders from place to place mending tin pots is the classic wandering, travelling worker.

clue.text: Well said: that was laid on with a ——" (As You Like It)

definitions.text: Well said: that was laid on with a ——" (As You Like It)

parts.words: Well said: that was laid on with a ——" (As You Like It)
parts.note: fill in Celia's line from As You Like It, a plasterer's tool for laying it on thick

explanation.walkthrough: Celia's line in As You Like It is 'Well said: that was laid on with a trowel', the source of the idiom for heavy flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: A plasterer's flat-bladed tool spreads mortar thickly, hence the phrase about overdone praise.

clue.text: This is what the engraver makes of Lionel

definitions.text: This is what the engraver makes of Lionel

indicators.note: what someone makes of a word here is a rearrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An engraver's portrait of a man called Lionel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes of' rearranges LIONEL; the whole clue also defines the black inlay engravers work with.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black metallic alloy rubbed into engraved lines on silver, the engraver's own inlay.

clue.text: Take it back

parts.note: withdraw a statement one has made, as a demand

explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a statement or belief formally, a retraction of words.

clue.text: The last person to invite to No Medals

definitions.text: The last person to invite to No Medals

parts.words: The last person to invite to No Medals
parts.note: an event where medals are banned would be wasted on a scholar of coins and medals

explanation.walkthrough: A party styled 'No Medals' would hardly suit someone whose whole study is coins and medals.
explanation.definitionFit: A numismatologist studies coins, tokens and medals, the very objects the party excludes.

clue.text: Class of type or type of class

definitions.meaning: an old printers' size of type, about nine point

explanation.definitionFit: Bourgeois is a nine-point printing size and also the propertied middle social rank.

clue.text: The other one of the twin beds, it seems

definitions.text: The other one of the twin beds, it seems

parts.words: The other one of the twin beds, it seems
parts.note: read literally, the companion bed is a 'fellow' to the first bed; the word means a partner

explanation.walkthrough: The word means an associate or partner, but read as 'bed fellow' it seems to be the matching bed in a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedfellow is someone who shares a bed, and by extension any close associate.

clue.text: Extremity of competitive oratory

definitions.meaning: the farthest point or highest degree
read as two words, speaking the greatest amount, as in a talking contest

explanation.definitionFit: The word means the farthest or greatest extreme; split, it is a contest to speak more than anyone.

clue.text: Salt water mostly fish

parts.note: a strait of sea water off Hampshire, whose name is mostly made of a flatfish's name

explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and the English mainland; its first four letters spell SOLE, a flatfish, so the name is 'mostly fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Solent is a named channel of sea between the Isle of Wight and Hampshire.

clue.text: How sweetly is the French marshal ordered to attend to his parting !

definitions.text: How sweetly is the French marshal ordered to attend to his parting !

parts.note: HO, an old call or exclamation like 'how!', is taken for the clue's 'How'
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
a hair parting is tidied with a comb

explanation.surface: A gushing compliment on a French marshal's neatly combed hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshal NEY is Napoleon's commander; you comb a parting. The whole clue also hints at the sweetly ordered cells of the finished product.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees store honey in neat rows of wax cells, a sweet thing laid out in order.

clue.text: But surely one might have a large helping ?

definitions.text: But surely one might have a large helping ?

parts.words: But surely one might have a large helping ?
parts.note: a word for something small and unimportant is also a pudding of which a big portion is welcome

explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a small, insignificant amount, yet the same word names a layered pudding of sponge, custard and cream, which one might eat in quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a paltry amount but also a British dessert served in generous bowlfuls.

clue.text: What's this about Ellen ? She doesn't seem to have been applauded.

annotationWithheld.why: What's this about Ellen ? She doesn't seem to have been applauded. (9): the wordplay HIST (anagram of THIS, also a hushing cry) around ELLEN gives the answer, but no clue words define a Greek scholar
annotationWithheld.clue: What's this about Ellen ? She doesn't seem to have been applauded.

clue.text: Garment made of a stuttering plum

parts.note: a stutterer repeats the opening sound, giving 'puh' before the word, spelt PE
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dress made from a plum, described with a stammer.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'plum' with a stutter: 'p-plum', written PE-PLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A peplum is a short flared overskirt or tunic flounce worn by women, so it is a piece of clothing.

clue.text: If they have a sense of duty they disregard it

definitions.text: If they have a sense of duty they disregard it

parts.words: If they have a sense of duty they disregard it
parts.note: the duty here is customs duty on goods, which certain traders deliberately evade

explanation.walkthrough: 'duty' looks moral, but it is customs duty, which those who run contraband ignore.
explanation.definitionFit: Smugglers bring goods in secretly to avoid paying the customs charges levied on them.

clue.text: It might beat an accompaniment to " the cock's shrill clarion "

definitions.text: It might beat an accompaniment to " the cock's shrill clarion "

parts.words: It might beat an accompaniment to " the cock's shrill clarion "
parts.note: a stick for beating a drum, and also the leg of a cooked bird such as a cock

explanation.walkthrough: 'the cock's shrill clarion' is from Gray's Elegy; the answer both beats a drum and is a cockerel's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumstick strikes a drum, and the same word names the lower leg of a cooked fowl.

clue.text: Ethelred's taken cover

annotationWithheld.why: Ethelred's taken cover (9): the answer is an anagram of ETHELRED'S, but no word signals the anagram; 'taken' is needed in the definition 'taken cover', so it cannot also be the indicator

clue.text: Dressy men of commerce whose spelling some schoolboys will quarrel with

definitions.text: Dressy men of commerce whose spelling some schoolboys will quarrel with

parts.words: Dressy men of commerce whose spelling some schoolboys will quarrel with
parts.note: clothiers who trade, and a London livery company whose school spells the name with a Y

explanation.walkthrough: The livery company of cloth merchants spells its name with an I, but its famous school, Merchant Taylors', uses a Y, so its pupils would dispute the spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchant tailors were tradesmen dealing in cloth and clothes, the dressy men of business.

clue.text: Medico in a high wind must take a chance

indicators.note: the medico is placed inside the word for the high wind

parts.note: a gale is a very strong wind
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor caught out in a storm has to risk it.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, the medical degree, stands for a doctor; it goes inside GALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To gamble is to risk something on an uncertain outcome.

clue.text: Something very wrong about air raid precautions turned upside down

annotationWithheld.why: Something very wrong about air raid precautions turned upside down (6): SIN around ARP reversed gives the letters, but no remaining clue word defines a wrenched joint ('Something very wrong' is used up as SIN)
annotationWithheld.clue: Something very wrong about air raid precautions turned upside down

clue.text: To' be detected in an American poncho richly embroidered

annotationWithheld.why: To be detected in an American poncho richly embroidered (6): the answer is hidden in 'poncho richly', but no clue word defines 'of a chorus'
annotationWithheld.clue: To' be detected in an American poncho richly embroidered

clue.text: Round a curve she aims up

indicators.note: the reversed word for aims goes round the curve
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to aim is to point at a target
an arc is a curve

explanation.surface: A woman aiming her shot over a curving path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the word for aims from the bottom up, making MIA; 'Round' says that wraps the curve, splitting it as M plus IA. Old clues often define a girl's name with just 'she'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcia is a female first name, so she is a typical woman in clue terms.

clue.text: This decoration may be what sends one to sleep in the sermon

definitions.text: This decoration may be what sends one to sleep in the sermon

parts.words: This decoration may be what sends one to sleep in the sermon
parts.note: a carved ornament on a church pew end, named after the seed pod of the flower that yields opium

explanation.walkthrough: The carved finial on a pew end is named after the seed head of the opium flower, so in church it might literally send a listener to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppyheads are carved finials topping the ends of church benches, named for the drowsy flower's seed capsule.

clue.text: Puppies all over the place

definitions.meaning: a dog's brood born at one time

explanation.definitionFit: A brood of newborn puppies is one sense; scattered refuse and mess is the other.

clue.text: Scar from Arctic ice

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of the following words, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frostbite mark picked up on a polar expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a light anagram signal: only ARCTIC is rearranged, to CICATR, and ICE stays in place at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicatrice is the healed mark left by a wound, another word for a scar.

clue.text: Shady business for a game

definitions.meaning: a court game played with a ball against walls

explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a swindling operation and also the walled-court ball game from which squash developed.

clue.text: One of the "sermons in stones" having grown feathers?

definitions.text: One of the "sermons in stones" having grown feathers?

parts.words: One of the "sermons in stones" having grown feathers?
parts.note: Shakespeare's 'sermons in stones' imagines stones talking; a stone's talk with wings is a small bird

explanation.walkthrough: In As You Like It there are 'sermons in stones'; a talk from a stone is a 'stone chat', and the stonechat is a small songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small European bird whose call sounds like two pebbles knocked together.
